results: IEEE 738 Drake example inputs -> 1025.4 A at 100 C (qc1 82.08, qc2 77.03, qcn 42.42, qr 39.11, qs 22.46 W/m; Hc 74.89 deg, Zc 113.95 deg, Qs 1027.3 W/m2, R(100) 9.390e-5 ohm/m).
CEA 2023 Table II (Zebra, Moose, Panther, Bersimis; Ta 40/45/48/50; Tc 75/85) reproduced within +/-1 A using the CEA AC resistances and full-normal solar (qs = alpha*S*D).
Satcon IS 398-2 table (Mole...Moose, 65/75 C) reproduced within +/-1 A using the printed AC resistances, Ta 40, V 0.61 m/s perpendicular, e=a=0.5, S=985 W/m2 normal.
Satcon AAAC table (34, 55, 100, 232 mm2) reproduced within +/-1 A with the same conditions.

Apar/Lumino IS 398-2 75/85 C values: match DC-based calc for 2-layer conductors (Wolf, Panther exactly); for 6/1 and 6/7 single-layer ACSR (Squirrel...Dog) DC-based calc is ~7% high - they match when R_ac = 1.15 x R_dc (the AC/DC ratio implied by Satcon/CEA tables for single-layer ACSR). Zebra/Moose need ~1.04.
Prysmian Drake/Cardinal/Partridge/Penguin 75 C (25 C amb, lat 30, July 1 noon) reproduced to 909/989/458/362 A vs 910/990/460/365 (computed Qs 1033 W/m2).

ieee738.standard: IEEE Std 738-2012 (superseded by IEEE 738-2023; 2023 changes not checked). Full text not accessed - equations below are taken from the PyPacity port of the IEEE 738 calculation program (pypacity) and arXiv:2607.23536 eqs 3-4, and verified by reproducing the Drake example and CEA/Satcon tables.
ieee738.units: SI; D0 in m, temperatures in C, q in W/m, I in A, R in ohm/m
ieee738.heat_balance: qc + qr = qs + I^2 * R(Tavg)  ->  I = sqrt((qc + qr - qs) / R(Tavg))
ieee738.resistance: R(T) = R(Tlow) + (R(Thigh) - R(Tlow)) / (Thigh - Tlow) * (T - Tlow)  (linear interpolation; Drake example uses R25 and R75)
ieee738.wind_direction_factor: K_angle = 1.194 - cos(phi) + 0.194*cos(2*phi) + 0.368*sin(2*phi)  (phi = angle between wind and conductor axis; =1.0 at 90 deg)
ieee738.convection_selection: qc = max(qc1, qc2, qcn)  (larger of the two forced values; then larger of forced vs natural)
ieee738.solar_heat_gain: qs = alpha * Qse * sin(theta) * A',  A' = D0 (projected area per metre)
ieee738.angle_of_incidence: theta = arccos[cos(Hc) * cos(Zc - Zl)]  (Zl = line azimuth)
ieee738.declination: delta = 23.46 * sin[(284 + N)/365 * 360 deg]  (N = day of year; pypacity uses 23.4583)
ieee738.solar_azimuth: Zc = C + arctan(chi), chi = sin(omega) / [sin(Lat)*cos(omega) - cos(Lat)*tan(delta)];  C = 0 if -180<=omega<0 and chi>=0; C = 180 if (-180<=omega<0 and chi<0) or (0<=omega<180 and chi>=0); C = 360 if 0<=omega<180 and chi<0
ieee738.solar_flux_sea_level: Qs = A + B*Hc + C*Hc^2 + D*Hc^3 + E*Hc^4 + F*Hc^5 + G*Hc^6  (Hc in degrees, W/m2)

Qs_coefficients_clear.source_note: pypacity prints rounded values (0.034692, -3.6112e-4, 1.9432e-6, -4.0761e-9); full-precision digits are from the IEEE 738-2012 table as commonly reproduced - verify against the standard

ieee738.validity_note: arXiv:2607.23536 quotes validated ranges for eqs (forced convection) of 15 C <= Ta <= 260 C and 21 C <= Ts <= 1004 C (as printed).

worked_example.inputs_source: arXiv:2607.23536 Table I (D, R25, R75, Tmax 100 C, e 0.8, a 0.8, azimuth 90 E-W, 0 m, 30 N, day 161); Ta 40 C and Vw 0.61 m/s perpendicular from pypacity demo() 'drawn from the IEEE 738 sample calculations'; 11:00 solar time from the user brief / common reproduction - not seen in the standard text.
worked_example.published_result_status: Not seen in an accessed source text (IEEE 738 paywalled). Stated in user brief; our implementation gives 1025.4 A, consistent.
worked_example.related: pypacity demo also uses (for a different case) lat 43 deg, measured solar 708.6 W/m2 and quotes 101.1 C at 1000 A for Drake.

notes: IS 398-2 table data come from manufacturer reproductions (Satcon, Lumino, Apar); the BIS original (law.resource.org copy) returned 404. Where they disagree it is noted per row.
The 6/1.96 (18 mm2) row in Lumino/Apar IS 398-2 tables has no code name ('---').

IS 398-2 vs BS 215 conductors with the same name and stranding have different R20 (e.g. Wolf 0.1871 vs 0.1828, Dog 0.2792 vs 0.2733) because of different resistivity/lay assumptions. Pick one standard per dataset.
Gopher, Ferret, Mink, Bear, Sheep are BS 215 / BS EN 50182 codes; they are not in the IS 398-2:1996 table. Goat and Lynx appear in Satcon's IS 398-2 table.
Indian tables' ampacities are computed with AC resistance; single-layer ACSR (6/1, 6/7) has AC/DC ~1.15 at 75 C in those tables. Using DC resistance over-predicts by ~7 %.
Solar in CEA/Apar tables is applied at 90 deg incidence: qs = alpha * S * D (no altitude/azimuth geometry, no elevation factor; elevation 0 m).
IEEE 738-2023 has superseded 2012; differences were not checked.
Nepal design ambient and max conductor temperature (NEA) remain unverified; CEA uses 45 C ambient (lower allowed for hilly areas).
Phase spacing for 11/33/132 kV in Nepal: not found; values null.
